newsitem.title: USA: Evidence to be re-read for Simpson jury.
newsitem.headline: Evidence to be re-read for Simpson jury.

text.p: The jury in O.J. Simpson's civil trial resumed its deliberations Tuesday after asking to hear again vital evidence in the case.

Simpson's testimony on what he was doing the night his ex-wife and her friend were murdered -- in particular what he was doing between between 9:45 p.m. and 11 p.m. -- was to be read back to the panel later Tuesday.

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend, Ronald Goldman, by a criminal court jury in 1995. He is currently battling a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the families of the victims who are seeking substantial damages.

The jury in the civil case, after deliberating for about 14 hours over three days last week, was ordered to start from scratch Friday by Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki after he dismissed the only black panellist for failing to disclose that her daughter worked in the Los Angeles County district attorney's office. The juror was replaced by an Asian-American man.

The reconstituted panel also asked for Simpson's responses to questions posed by plaintiffs' attorney John Kelly, who represents the estate of Nicole Brown Simpson, on the Jan. 1, 1989, violent argument between Simpson and his then-wife, which left her bruised and battered.

On the witness stand, Simpson said he never hit his ex-wife on that occasion but took "full responsibility" for her injuries. The jury also wants to re-hear the account of Simpson's longtime friend, Al Cowlings, who testified that he took Nicole Brown Simpson to a hospital for treatment following the incident.

In addition, the jury asked to hear again the testimony of Allan Park, the limousine driver who testified that he arrived at Simpson's mansion at about 10:22 p.m. on the night of the murders but could not raise Simpson until about 10:55 p.m.
Finally, they asked to re-hear the tape of Simpson's interview with two detectives on the day after the murders.
